# FileHandle descriptor and queued close ownership

FileHandleLease contains the single actual descriptor. Adoption transfers that owner only after fallible method/name allocation. A FileHandle state retains its existing numeric fd as an observation; it does not close by that number. Explicit synchronous close and abandoned-handle finalization consume the lease before calling libc, preserving libuv EINTR/EINPROGRESS no-retry policy and actual error status.

Queued CloseHandle work takes the lease before work-queue publication. Worker Run closes that lease, and completion retires the observed fd. Failed queue admission/destruction and cancellation before Run return the unperformed lease to the still-rooted parent. Cancellation after Run cannot restore an already-consumed descriptor. No lease operation invokes JS, duplicates an fd, reopens a pathname or alters the OFD.

This is a consumed prerequisite for transfer, not public transfer activation. The public pinned transfer hooks remain deliberately removed by build.py. Native clone callbacks still support MessagePort moves only. The next coherent slice must add a real FileHandle clone tag/packet sidecar, native admission/commit, target-local native error factory, init/abrupt-completion and abort ownership, registered public FileHandle construction, and packet/Worker-exit cleanup. Receiver init may close reentrantly; rollback must respect queued close ownership and must never close a reused numeric descriptor. Registered JavaScript transfer order and partial-detachment semantics must remain unchanged.

Workers use native threads in the same guest process, so transfer must move the same descriptor/OFD, not introduce a process fd-table or kernel ABI change. This source statement does not prove guest pthread fd-table or four-host behavior. Unmanaged descriptor tracking, fd reuse after outside raw fs.close, full StreamBase/FileHandle readableWebStream behavior, abort and target realm/GC/Worker conformance remain separate obligations.
